Previous reports had indicated that Apple had cancelled plans for an all-glass iPhone designed to celebrate the 20th anniversary of the iPhone. According to a Bloomberg report, the redesigned new device is still set to launch next year as scheduled, and will be applied to the Pro models. Details are as follows.

Bloomberg says the redesign plans are proceeding as scheduled

Earlier today, investment analysis firm Jefferies downgraded Apple stock, citing its supply chain investigation showing that Apple had cancelled an all-glass iPhone project originally scheduled for launch next year to celebrate the iPhone's 20th anniversary.

Bloomberg now reports that the company "is expected to launch an iPhone Pro model with a new glass design next year," adding that "the front and back of the phone will use glass—with internal codenames V73 and V74 respectively—and the glass material will extend to both sides of the device, connected in the middle by a metal frame."

However, the report also points out that the plan has undergone multiple revisions since its original conception:

The report further directly refutes the analysis issued by Jefferies earlier today, stating that "Apple's product roadmap has not changed."

Jefferies's account

Earlier today, Jefferies analyst Edison Lee said that, based on the firm's supply chain investigation, the all-glass iPhone had been cancelled due to poor production yields.

Lee described this development as a "significant setback" for Apple's efforts to launch higher-priced iPhones amid rising memory costs, and noted that cancelling the plan could affect Apple's ability to raise the average selling price and gross margin of Pro models.

Jefferies accordingly downgraded Apple stock, lowering its target price from US$285.56 to US$263.66. Prior to this, the firm had already cut its target price from US$308.92 on 31 July, after Apple announced its fiscal year 2026 third-quarter results and issued harsh guidance for the fourth quarter.
